title: First Flight
summary: A guided tour of the portal for each role.

personas.label: New contributor
personas.summary: Build a safe mental model before touching application code.
personas.outcome: You can identify the owning application, tell existing from planned behaviour, run the basic commands and prepare a small change.

stops.title: Check a page before trusting it
stops.instruction: Check the page status, verification date and sources before you follow a procedure.
stops.why: Each page separates existing behaviour from planned behaviour.

stops.title: Map the four surfaces
stops.instruction: Locate the storefront, admin, API, and developer portal responsibilities.
stops.why: A correct first change starts with the application that owns the behaviour.

stops.title: Follow dependencies inward
stops.instruction: Trace UI and edge concerns toward ports and the core domain.
stops.why: The dependency rule is the fastest test for whether a proposed change belongs in the right layer.

stops.title: Interpret lifecycle labels
stops.instruction: Learn what implemented, scaffolded, planned, deferred and deprecated mean, and why they are not percentages.
stops.why: A page's status tells you whether the behaviour it describes exists.

stops.title: Learn the safe command surface
stops.instruction: Identify the package-manager, workspace, build, test, and portal commands used by this repository.
stops.why: The repository's own commands keep your environment consistent.

stops.title: Finish a change properly
stops.instruction: Use the documentation pull-request checklist to prepare a reviewable handoff.
stops.why: Code, docs and tests change together.

personas.label: Frontend developer
personas.summary: Trace a customer or operator interaction through Angular routing, state, data, and verification.
personas.outcome: You can choose the correct frontend surface, state owner, server-data boundary, and definition-of-done checks for a change.

stops.title: Learn the frontend stack
stops.instruction: Review which state tools each application uses, and which data comes from the API or JSON files.
stops.why: Know which state and data tools each application uses.

stops.title: Orient inside the storefront
stops.instruction: Map a public experience from the file-based page into feature and data-access layers.
stops.why: Pages stay thin, and behaviour lives in the feature that owns it.

stops.title: Trace filename to URL
stops.instruction: Follow the Analog file-based routing convention before adding or moving a customer route.
stops.why: Route ownership determines rendering, data loading, and browser-only safety.

stops.title: Choose the state owner
stops.instruction: Use the decision table to distinguish server state, complex client mutation, and local feature state.
stops.why: TanStack Query, classic NgRx, and SignalStore solve different ownership problems.

stops.title: Compare the operator surface
stops.instruction: Review how admin routes, feature families, and services differ from the public storefront.
stops.why: Storefront and admin share contracts and conventions, but they do not share every interaction or state boundary.

stops.title: Check a frontend change
stops.instruction: Finish with the architecture, behaviour, rendering, interaction and verification checks.
stops.why: A change must handle loading, failure, keyboard and server rendering.

personas.label: Backend developer
personas.summary: Trace a request from its validated contract through the domain ports, adapters, persistence and open decisions.
personas.outcome: You can place a backend change in the right layer and know what completes it.

stops.title: Learn the dependency direction
stops.instruction: Read the controller-to-port-to-use-case-to-adapter flow before opening implementation files.
stops.why: Provider and persistence concerns must remain replaceable at the edges.

stops.title: Map the backend platform
stops.instruction: Identify the six architectural boundaries and the responsibilities between them.
stops.why: The atlas provides the shared vocabulary used by request, contract, domain, and persistence documentation.

stops.title: Separate the four shapes
stops.instruction: Distinguish transport contracts, domain types, persistence models, and response serialization.
stops.why: Shape leakage is a common way to accidentally couple the core to an adapter.

stops.title: Read the port boundary
stops.instruction: Check what the core may depend on and how edge capabilities are expressed as ports.
stops.why: A swappable edge begins with a stable inward-facing contract.

stops.title: Trace a real request
stops.instruction: Follow the request path, and compare it with the target design before you propose a new stage.
stops.why: The trace shows what each stage of a request does.

stops.title: Explore the collections
stops.instruction: Use the map to tell existing collections from planned ones.
stops.why: The map separates existing collections from planned ones.

stops.title: Check open decisions
stops.instruction: Check open decisions and what they affect before you build on them.
stops.why: Do not assume an answer to an open product or architecture decision.

personas.label: Platform operator
personas.summary: Move through scope, configuration, health checks, local persistence and recovery.
personas.outcome: You can tell a successful build from a healthy deployment, and know what to check before running a procedure.

stops.title: Start with the scope
stops.instruction: Identify which procedures are available and which are planned.
stops.why: The page states which operations are available and which are planned.

stops.title: Map environment and services
stops.instruction: Review local configuration, Docker Mongo replica-set assumptions, and browser runtime config.
stops.why: The applications expect these supporting services.

stops.title: Separate secrets from public config
stops.instruction: Trace how server secrets and public browser configuration each reach the running application.
stops.why: Browser bundles must never receive server credentials or provider secrets.

stops.title: Review available operations
stops.instruction: Separate the tools that exist from the deployment work that remains.
stops.why: Know which tools and jobs exist.

stops.title: Read the health endpoints
stops.instruction: Tell liveness from readiness, and learn what each endpoint checks.
stops.why: A responsive process can still be unable to serve real traffic.

stops.title: Verify the local Mongo lifecycle
stops.instruction: Review the single-node replica-set commands and what each one reports.
stops.why: Transaction-capable topology and application connectivity require separate checks.

stops.title: Enter recovery through symptoms
stops.instruction: Use the troubleshooting tables to move from a symptom to its likely cause and fix.
stops.why: Start recovery from the symptom.
